title: User manuals for machinery and equipment
description: Manuals, often produced in electronic or traditional formats, allow users to quickly find specific information without having to leaf through lengthy texts.

blocks.text: The main objectives of creating a user manual from RECON’s perspective:
Manuals, often produced in electronic or traditional formats, allow users to quickly find specific information without having to leaf through lengthy texts.

items: Safety: Providing information on safe usage rules to prevent accidents.
Correct operation: Guiding the user step by step to facilitate installation and operation.
Legal requirements: Providing the required technical documentation, particularly when launching products onto the market.
Minimising breakdowns: Maintenance tips extend the service life of the equipment.
Reducing operating costs: Technical support becomes less necessary when the user can find answers in the manual.

blocks.text: Structure of the user manual (What it must contain)
The manual should guide the user through the entire life cycle of the machine:

items: Title page: Machine name, model, type, CE marking, manufacturer’s details. Introduction/General information: Intended use of the machine, EC Declaration of Conformity (or a copy thereof), original manual (if this is a translation).
Safety (Health and Safety) – key section: Warnings, pictograms, description of residual risks, required personal protective equipment.
Technical description: Construction, main components, operating principle, technical parameters (drawings, diagrams).
Operation: Start-up/shutdown procedures, normal operation, and abnormal situations.

blocks.text: These instructions usually take the form of Safety Work Instructions (IBWR), which the contractor draws up. Mandatory structure of the instructions
Writing guidelines

items: Simple language: We avoid technical jargon wherever possible. We write briefly, concisely and unambiguously. Step-by-step structure: Use numbered lists for procedures (1, 2, 3...) and bullet points for features. Tailor to the target audience: Different language for a maintenance technician, different for an operator.
Visualisation: We use photos, technical drawings and diagrams instead of long descriptions.
Visibility of warnings: We clearly highlight risks to life or health (e.g. a box, red colour, the word "DANGER"). Warning pictograms are essential.

Standards: Compliance with the new Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 (from 2027) or the Machinery Directive 2006/42/EC. Health and safety content: The instructions must include information on ‘foreseeable misuse’.

blocks.text: Development process (Work stages)
Analysis
Understanding the machine, discussions with its designers and operator.
Sketching
Gathering drawings, diagrams and technical documentation.
Writing
Creating content (ideally whilst testing the machine – this helps to spot errors in the description).
Visualisation
Adding photos/drawings and describing them.
Verification
Having the instructions checked by a third party (e.g. a health and safety officer or another operator).
Publication
PDF format or a printed version included with the device.
